content.user_title: Diagnose Errors with the TRACE Framework
content.value_statement: Complex failures can hide their root cause behind noisy stack traces and secondary symptoms. Error Detective organizes evidence, tests hypotheses, and verifies targeted fixes.
actual_capabilities: Applies the Trace, Read, Analyze, Check, and Execute workflow to software failures.
Interprets Python, JavaScript, Java, and Go stack traces and identifies relevant application frames.
Classifies syntax, runtime, logic, integration, performance, and configuration errors.
Builds testable hypotheses from error messages, code context, environment details, and application state.
Provides a local helper for parsing logs, summarizing error patterns, and recording debug sessions.
limitations: Results depend on complete error messages, reproduction steps, and relevant code context.
The skill cannot inspect live systems or production state without user-provided access and data.
Reference examples do not replace language, framework, or service documentation.
The optional helper reads local log files and writes session records under .debug_sessions when explicitly run.

use_cases.title: Triage an application failure
use_cases.description: Turn a stack trace and reproduction steps into a prioritized root-cause investigation.

use_cases.title: Investigate a production incident
use_cases.description: Organize logs, environment differences, impact, and hypotheses before selecting a controlled fix.

use_cases.title: Review a debugging approach
use_cases.description: Check whether a proposed fix addresses the root cause and includes useful regression tests.

prompt_templates.title: Explain an error
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply TRACE to this error message: [error]. Explain the error type, likely cause, and first three checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis of one error message

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a stack trace
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this stack trace: [trace]. Identify the first relevant application frame, separate symptoms from causes, and list missing context.

prompt_templates.title: Build a debugging plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these reproduction steps, logs, and code excerpts: [details]. Rank hypotheses, define one test per hypothesis, and avoid changing multiple variables.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a production fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this incident evidence and proposed fix: [details]. Challenge the root-cause claim, assess side effects, and design verification and regression coverage.

output_examples.input: A Python AttributeError occurs when a user opens a profile page.
output: Category: runtime error caused by a missing object.
Primary hypothesis: some users do not have an associated profile.
Next checks: inspect the failing frame, compare affected records, and verify the profile creation path.

output_examples.input: A cart update sometimes fails after the server returns an error response.
output: Root cause: the client assumes every response contains an item list.
Fix direction: check the response status and validate the response shape before updating state.
Verification: test success, server error, malformed response, timeout, and rapid updates.

output_examples.input: A failure appears only in production after a dependency update.
output: Compare dependency versions, configuration, data shape, permissions, and load between environments.
Test the dependency change as one isolated hypothesis.
Record evidence before rollback or remediation.

best_practices: Capture the complete error, relevant context, and reliable reproduction steps before changing code.
Test one specific hypothesis at a time and record whether evidence confirms or rejects it.
Verify the original failure, related behavior, edge cases, and regression coverage after the fix.
anti_patterns: Do not patch the visible symptom before tracing the originating failure.
Do not change several variables at once because the effective fix becomes unclear.
Do not expose credentials, personal data, or production secrets in logs shared for analysis.

faq.question: What does TRACE mean?
faq.answer: TRACE means Trace, Read, Analyze, Check, and Execute. Each stage moves from evidence collection to a verified fix.

faq.question: Which languages can it help debug?
faq.answer: The guidance is general. Included parser examples cover Python, JavaScript, Java, and Go stack traces.

faq.question: Does it automatically modify my code?
faq.answer: No. It recommends focused changes, but code edits depend on the tools and permissions available in your session.

faq.question: Can it analyze production incidents?
faq.answer: Yes, when you provide sanitized logs, impact details, environment context, and reproduction evidence.

faq.question: What does the helper script store?
faq.answer: Explicit session commands store descriptions, notes, timestamps, and solutions in local JSON files under .debug_sessions.

faq.question: How should sensitive logs be handled?
faq.answer: Remove credentials, tokens, personal data, and confidential values before sharing logs or stack traces.
